signInAgain.body: Changing redirect URIs, making a new secret or deleting an app needs a sign-in from the last {{minutes}} minutes. That way, nobody else who has your session can take over your app.

metadata.title: Developer terms | Boardsesh for developers
metadata.description: The terms an app accepts when it registers to connect to Boardsesh accounts.

terms.title: Boardsesh developer terms

draftNotice.title: Draft, not in force
draftNotice.body: The Boardsesh team has not approved these terms yet. They may change before any app connects to a real climber’s account.

terms.intro: These terms apply to anyone who registers an app that connects to Boardsesh accounts through the Boardsesh API. You accept them when you register an app, for yourself and for everyone who works on the app with you.

items.purpose: Use what a climber shares only for the features they connected your app for.
items.noSale: Don’t sell or rent it, and don’t share it with anyone for advertising, profiling or data brokering.
items.setterClimbs: A tick comes with the climb it is on, including a draft or an unlisted climb someone else set. That detail is there so the climber can see their own logbook. Don’t publish it, show it to other people or build a list of climbs from it.
items.delete: Delete a climber’s Boardsesh data when they disconnect your app or ask you to, unless they ask you to keep it.
items.privacyPolicy: Have a privacy policy that says what you do with Boardsesh data, and register its link with your app. Climbers see it before they approve.
items.security: Keep tokens and client secrets on your server or in the device’s secure storage, never in a URL or a log. If you learn that one leaked, or that someone reached climbers’ data without permission, tell us at legal@boardsesh.com within 72 hours.

items.limits: Stay within the rate limits, and wait as long as Retry-After says.
items.scopes: Ask only for the scopes you use. Don’t try to get around a scope, a limit, a suspension or a climber’s choices.
items.catalog: Don’t use the API to copy Boardsesh’s climb catalogue. The public nightly snapshots are there for that.
items.service: Board control, sessions and the climb catalogue are not part of the API. An app whose accounts, climbing, board control or sessions run on Boardsesh’s servers needs our written permission, which we don’t currently give.

items.worksWith: Say that your app works with Boardsesh, for example “Works with Boardsesh” or “Import your Boardsesh logbook”. Don’t suggest that Boardsesh made, reviewed or endorses your app.
items.ownName: Don’t use Boardsesh, or anything that looks like it, in your app’s name, publisher name or icon.
items.boardBrands: Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard and other board names belong to their owners. Use them only to say which board a climb is on, and don’t suggest that a board maker endorses your app or Boardsesh.

items.suspend: Suspend or delete an app that breaks these terms, puts climbers at risk or overloads the service. When we suspend an app, the console shows you the reason.
items.changes: Change the API under the versioning rules in the developer docs, and change these terms. The console shows the new version, and the next app you register accepts it.
items.asIs: The API is provided as it is, with no promise that it is always available or free of errors.

ending.title: Stopping
ending.body: You can delete your app in the console at any time, and every climber’s connection to it ends at once. Then delete the Boardsesh data you hold, unless a climber asked you to keep theirs.

metadata.title: Read a climber's logbook with the Boardsesh API
metadata.description: Register an app, send the climber to approve it, then read their logbook: a full download first, then only what changed. Scopes, limits and errors on one page.

docs.title: Connect an app to a climber's logbook
docs.lead: Let a training planner, a logbook or your own script read a climber's Boardsesh ticks once they approve it. They can disconnect it at any time.

invitation.title: Registration is by invitation
invitation.body: Early access is open only to developer accounts the Boardsesh team has added. Each app can have {{live}} climbers connected at once and {{perDay}} new ones in any 24 hours. To ask for access, write to {{email}} and say what your app does.

open.title: Register your app
open.body: Sign in as an enabled developer, accept the developer terms and create an app in the console. You get a client ID straight away, and a client secret if your server exchanges the code. If your account isn't enabled yet, the console says so.

items.read: Read every tick the climber has logged, on every board, including ticks they keep private on Boardsesh.
items.sync: Download the whole logbook once, then fetch only what changed. A change usually shows up within a second.
items.profile: Read their display name and avatar, if you ask for that scope.
items.disconnect: The climber can disconnect your app at any time in Settings, Connected apps. Your next call then fails, and you delete what you stored.
items.notYet: Reading the logbook is the only thing live today. Workouts and webhooks are not available yet.

items.register: Register an app in the developer console and keep the client ID.
items.approve: Send the climber to the authorize URL in their system browser. They sign in and tap Allow.
items.exchange: Swap the code your redirect URI receives for an access token and a refresh token.
items.snapshot: Call the changes endpoint with no cursor and follow every page until hasMore is false. That is the full logbook.
items.feed: From then on, call it with your last cursor to get new, edited and deleted ticks.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.lead: Ask for the smallest set you need. The consent screen lists each one in plain words.

items.logbook: Every tick on every board, including ones the climber keeps private.
items.offline: A refresh token, so you can keep reading while the climber is away. It opens no data by itself.

items.consent: An app without a client secret, and every native app, shows the consent screen on every authorization. prompt=none never returns a code; it returns error=consent_required. Keep the refresh token instead of authorizing again. Only a confidential web app with an https redirect is remembered.
items.redirect: Redirect URIs match as exact strings, up to {{max}} per app. Use https, a loopback address (http://127.0.0.1 or http://[::1], port ignored) or a private-use scheme with a dot in it. http://localhost and wildcards are refused.
items.redirectChange: Adding or replacing a redirect URI asks every climber who approved your app to approve it again. Removing one, or editing the name or links, does not. Tokens you already hold keep working until the climber is asked again.
items.recentSignIn: Adding, replacing or removing a redirect URI, rotating the client secret and deleting an app each need a sign-in within the last {{minutes}} minutes. If yours is older, the console asks you to sign in again.
items.notice: You get an email when redirect URIs change, the secret rotates, an app is deleted or a new app is registered on your account.
items.pkce: PKCE with S256 is required for every app. Send resource=https://api.boardsesh.com/v1 when you authorize, exchange a code and refresh. Tokens issued without it are refused by the API.
items.code: A code lasts {{seconds}} seconds and works once. Sending it twice also ends the tokens it issued, so restart authorization instead of retrying.
items.tokens: An access token lasts 1 hour. A refresh token lasts {{days}} days and changes on every use: store the new one before you use the new access token, and never refresh for one climber in parallel.
items.signin: A climber who last signed in more than 30 days ago, or before their last password change, signs in again before the consent screen.
items.disconnect: If a climber disconnects, resets their password or deletes their account, the API answers 401 invalid_token and a refresh answers invalid_grant. Show a Reconnect Boardsesh state, stop calling for that climber and delete what you stored.

requests.title: A first connection
requests.lead: Open the authorize URL in the system browser, never in an embedded web view. Swap in your own client ID, redirect URI, state and code.
requests.exchange: Your redirect URI gets a code. Exchange it:
requests.sync: Then read the logbook. Leave cursor out the first time and follow the cursor in each answer. Sync when the climber opens your app, and in the background no more than every 15 minutes per climber.
requests.confidential: A confidential app, one that keeps a client secret on its server, also sends client_secret in the body (client_secret_post) or as HTTP Basic (client_secret_basic), whichever it registered. A public app sends only client_id.

items.api: API: {{climber}} requests a minute per climber and {{app}} a minute per app.
items.token: Token endpoint: {{refresh}} refreshes a minute per climber, and {{exchange}} code exchanges or revokes a minute per app per client IP.
items.fullSync: Starting a full download: 2 a minute per climber. A 503 with Retry-After on a download means wait at least that long.
items.page: limit runs from 1 to 200 and defaults to 100. A page can be empty and still have hasMore: true.
items.history: Changes are kept for 90 days. An older cursor answers 410 cursor_expired; start a full download without a cursor.
items.body: A request body over 64 KB answers 413.
items.caps: Early access: {{apps}} apps per developer account, and per app {{live}} climbers connected at once and {{perDay}} new ones in 24 hours.
items.headers: Every response carries Boardsesh-Request-Id and RateLimit headers. A 429 carries Retry-After in seconds.

errors.title: Errors
errors.lead: Errors are JSON with error, message and requestId. Branch on the HTTP status first; new codes can appear.

items.invalidToken: The access token expired or was revoked. Refresh once and retry. If the refresh fails, ask the climber to reconnect.
items.insufficientScope: The token doesn't carry the scope this call needs.
items.cursorExpired: The cursor is too old or no longer valid. Start a full download without a cursor.
items.rateLimited: Over a limit. Wait for the seconds in Retry-After.
items.busy: Boardsesh is busy or paused app access for a moment. Wait for Retry-After and retry. It never means the climber disconnected.

versioning.title: Versions
versioning.body: The version is in the path, /v1. New fields, routes, scopes and enum values arrive on v1 without notice, so read what you know and ignore the rest. Removing or renaming a field becomes v2, and v1 keeps running for at least six months with a Sunset header on every response.
